rationale: Central environment-driven configuration class for the backend, used across modules for the database URL, secrets, token expiry, SMTP and Sentry. It is a cohesive, widely depended-on application unit with validation logic, not a domain schema or infrastructure artifact. It only declares settings consumed elsewhere and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Generated TanStack Router type interface in routeTree.gen.ts listing root child routes. It is generated boilerplate typing, not a route entry or navigation graph itself. The routes it references are modelled from the route files, so this symbol is not an architectural element.

A shadcn/ui-style sidebar primitive: a styled button slot that is reusable and has no callers. It is a generic library component definition in the design-system ui folder, so it is a minor UX building block rather than an application-specific control.

FastAPI router module grouping utility endpoints under /utils (test-email, health-check). As a whole it is an API route group, best fit as a path-level grouping in the API layer. It is minor utility surface. Auth and email sending are delegated to dependencies and helpers, so the module itself implements no concerns.

HTTP GET route handler for /users/{user_id}, which makes it an API operation contract. It enforces an inline privilege check (self or superuser, otherwise 403) and reads the User entity from the database session. It is a significant endpoint on the users API surface.

SQLModel ORM entity (table=True) defining the persisted User record with id, hashed password, timestamp and items relationship. Per the spec, an ORM model is a data-model objectschema that maps to a data-store collection. It is a core domain entity, so significance is 3.

Generated SDK client method bound to POST /api/v1/login/test-token with a bearer security scheme. The api layer treats generated client methods as evidence for one Operation. It issues an HTTP call to the backend and carries bearer-token credentials, so authentication and external integration apply. It is a generated leaf with no callers, hence moderate significance.

FastAPI route handler for PATCH /me/password, making it an API operation. It verifies the current password credential and hashes the new one, which is authentication work, and commits the updated user record to the database session. It is a notable endpoint, though not a core entry point.

A TypeScript props interface for the DeleteUser React component, consisting only of an id and an onSuccess callback. It is component scaffolding below the granularity of an architecture element. The component itself might be modelled in the ux layer, but its props type is not.

Private config validation helper that warns or raises when a secret still has the placeholder value 'changethis'. It is security hygiene, but at the level of an implementation detail inside Settings validation, not a modelled element on its own. It does not authenticate or authorize anything.

HTTP GET route on the users router that lists users with pagination. It is an API operation contract (one method-path pair). The handler queries the User table directly via the session. Authorization is likely applied through router dependencies (superuser check), not in this symbol.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts Axios HTTP client runtime. It is generic generated boilerplate rather than an application-specific architectural element, although it performs outbound HTTP calls. At most it is incidental evidence for an API client; it is not modelled on its own.

A trivial TypeScript props interface with a single field typing the ItemActionsMenu component's input. It is implementation detail of the UI component rather than an architectural element. The component itself would be modelled in the ux layer, not its props type.

A non-table SQLModel defining the login response payload (access_token, token_type). FastAPI publishes it as a schema in OpenAPI, so it is a data-model object schema. It only carries the token and performs no identity verification itself. It is notable as the auth response contract.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts utility module for serializing path/query parameters into URL strings. It is generated boilerplate and a formatting helper below the granularity of an architectural element, so it is not modelled.

A generated API client method bound to POST /api/v1/login/access-token. The spec counts generated client methods as evidence for API operations. It performs the OAuth2 password-form token request that authenticates the user, over HTTP to the backend. Being generated, it mirrors the backend route, so significance is moderate.

This is the root route's render component in TanStack Router: an application shell that renders head content and the Outlet for child routes, plus devtools. Per the spec, a framework layout that renders an outlet is modelled as a View. It is structurally central but contains almost no logic, so significance is moderate.
